parameters.antarctic_rule: no WorldCover south of 60S: cells <= 1 m treated as water; windows never nominated

datasets.earth_dem: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 COG, s3://copernicus-dem-90m (release as served on run date)

known_coverage_limits: windows never cross 1-degree tile seams; cells within ~1.6 km of a seam have no 3.2 km-baseline slope
tiles north/south of ~84.5 deg are narrower than a 10 km window
cells under trees, crops, buildings, water or wetland (WorldCover) are masked; a cell's 3.2 km disc must be fully unmasked
Antarctica: no land cover; recorded for coverage only

references.name: Jezero crater floor: olivine cumulate (Seitah formation) and serpentinized igneous rock (Maaz formation)
references.site_note: Two different Mars rocks. Seitah is an olivine cumulate, weakly altered, with small amounts of Mg-Fe carbonate. The in situ serpentinization evidence (Tosca 2025) is from the overlying Maaz formation, a pyroxene-plagioclase igneous unit, not from the Seitah cumulate. An Earth serpentinite combines the Seitah rock type with the Maaz process; no single Mars site in these sources shows both.
not_comparable: Fe-rich (Mars) vs Mg-rich (Earth mantle) olivine and serpentine: Fe-olivine yields Fe-serpentine and about five times more H2 than terrestrial peridotite (Tutolo2023)
humid weathering and vegetation on Earth

properties.statement: olivine cumulate (olivine-rich ultramafic rock); pyroxenite/hornblendite/gabbro are different rocks
abundant millimetre olivine

serpentinization of olivine in Maaz rocks, interpreted from in situ mineralogy and chemistry
hydrogen production is inferred from the serpentinization reaction; it was not measured
